jobs.prompt:
Review release train 3 of Project Swarm: branch swarm/train3 against main at 60de9058 (1.167.25). The combined code diff (236 files, 51 reviewed D-fix PRs plus the train-3 core work) is in your context at coordination/review/train3.diff; the full workspace is also present, so open any file you need before judging.

What changed:
(1) D-fix silent-catch audit (g-33a7a4ae): about 200 previously silent catches across roughly 100 tool modules now log a bounded message. Sensitive areas: locks (tools/base-check-lock.mjs, tools/projects.mjs, tools/integration-lock.mjs), money (tools/gpu-commands.mjs, tools/brain-commands.mjs, tools/project-commands.mjs), kill/process (tools/gpu-commands.mjs, tools/claude-shell.mjs), privacy (tools/errors.mjs, tools/tickets.mjs, tools/security-review.mjs), sandbox (tools/claude-shell.mjs).
(2) tools/lane-health.mjs: persist writes are serialized behind a queue with flush/stop and no fire-and-forget last write.
(3) tools/managers/visual-qa/screenshots.mjs: atomicWrite no longer closes its handle twice when rename fails; original error still rethrown and tmp cleanup unchanged.
(4) tools/swarm.mjs: swarm ask with an empty --context file no longer crashes reading costUsd.
(5) Tests: five load-flaky tests fixed at the root (concurrency-guard Ctrl-C path, handbuild chat-merge hook, field-lessons m2 salvage, local-lane slot release, lane-health persistence), with no retries or quarantine; 24 Phase 2 lock-race tests plus 8 tests recorded as todo for real lock bugs (base-check-lock, projects, integration-lock).
(6) New tools/stress-tests.mjs and npm run test:stress: reruns the previously flaky files for 5 rounds at concurrency 8, fails fast with child output; STRESS_ROUNDS and STRESS_CONCURRENCY override.
(7) Version/changelog/lock at 1.167.26.

Pass bar (owner): blockers only. Look hard for: a guard or approval bypass; money spent past a cap or on a paused lane; a key or secret reaching a paused lane or a log; wrong commits on protected branches; data loss (locks, review records, ledgers); a crash on a normal path; a regression to existing behavior; a log that leaks secrets, tokens, private names or file contents; a test weakened, skipped, retried or quarantined so a real failure can hide; a todo entry that masks a failure that should be fixed here. Everything else is a follow-up. For the D-fix batches, verify logging-only discipline: no control-flow, return value, fallback, throw or export change, silent only for the expected benign codes, and every catch binding really used.

Write ONLY coordination/review/train3-review.json: {"verdict":"pass"|"fail","score":0-10,"blockers":[{"file":"","line":0,"problem":"","exploit_or_failure":"","fix":""}],"followups":[same shape],"summary":""}. verdict is fail only if blockers is non-empty.
